title: The evolution and developmental dynamics of histone-based chromatin regulation in Annelida
authors: Martín-Zamora FM; Cole J; Donnellan RD; Guynes K; Carrillo-Baltodano AM; Dickman MJ; Hurd PJ; Martín-Durán JM
one_liner_zh: 该文研究环节动物组蛋白修饰与染色质调控的演化，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作建模、结合位点预测或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: Eukaryotic histones protect and package nuclear DNA into nucleosomes. The dynamic addition and removal of posttranslational modifications on these proteins define regulatory regions that play a central role in genome and chromatin biology. However, our understanding of these regulatory mechanisms in animals is largely based on a few model systems, which prevents a general understanding of how histone-based regulation unfolds and promotes phenotypic variation during animal embryogenesis. Here, we apply a comprehensive multi-omics approach to dissect the histone-based regulatory complement in Annelida, one of the largest invertebrate phyla. Annelids exhibit a conserved histone repertoire organised in clusters of dynamically regulated, hyperaccessible chromatin. However, unlike other animals with reduced genomes, the worm Dimorphilus gyrociliatus shows a dramatically streamlined histone repertoire, revealing that genome compaction has lineage-specific effects on histone-based regulation. Notably, the annelid Owenia fusiformis has two H2A.X variants that co-occur in other animals, whose functional implications are unclear but represent a unique case of widespread parallel evolution of a histone variant in Eukarya. Histone-modifying enzyme complements are largely conserved amongst annelids. Yet, temporal differences in the expression of a reduced set of histone modifiers correlate with distinct ontogenetic traits and variation in the adult landscapes of histone modifications, as revealed by quantitative mass spectrometry in O. fusiformis and Capitella teleta . Collectively, our unparalleled analysis of histone-based epigenetics within a non-model phylum informs the evolution of histone-based regulation, presenting a framework to explore how this fundamental genome regulatory layer contributes to developmental and morphological diversification in annelids and animals generally.
abstract_zh: 真核生物组蛋白将核DNA保护并包装成核小体。这些蛋白质上翻译后修饰的动态添加和移除定义了调控区域，在基因组和染色质生物学中发挥核心作用。然而，我们对动物中这些调控机制的理解主要基于少数模式系统，这阻碍了对基于组蛋白的调控如何在动物胚胎发生过程中展开并促进表型变异的普遍理解。在此，我们采用全面的多组学方法，解析环节动物门（Annelida）——最大的无脊椎动物门之一——中基于组蛋白的调控组成。环节动物表现出保守的组蛋白库，组织成动态调控、高可及性染色质的簇。然而，与其他基因组缩减的动物不同，蠕虫Dimorphilus gyrociliatus显示出显著精简的组蛋白库，揭示基因组压缩对基于组蛋白的调控具有谱系特异性效应。值得注意的是，环节动物Owenia fusiformis具有两种H2A.X变体，这些变体在其他动物中共存，其功能意义尚不明确，但代表了真核生物中组蛋白变体广泛平行进化的独特案例。组蛋白修饰酶的组成在环节动物中大体保守。然而，通过O. fusiformis和Capitella teleta的定量质谱分析揭示，一组减少的组蛋白修饰因子在表达上的时间差异与不同的个体发育特征及成体组蛋白修饰景观的变异相关。总体而言，我们对非模式门类中基于组蛋白的表观遗传学的无与伦比的分析，为基于组蛋白的调控进化提供了信息，并提出了一个框架，以探索这一基本基因组调控层如何促进环节动物及一般动物的发育和形态多样化。
